title: The Soul Field (_S)

canonical_node.axiom: The soul (_S) is a real, localized, persistent information pattern in the chi-field that constitutes personal identity and survives physical death.
definitions: Soul (_S): A coherent information pattern in the chi-field.
chi-field: The fundamental information field (Logos field).
Localized: Having specific identity and boundaries within the chi-field.
Persistent: Continuing through time without cessation.
Identity: The continuity of the soul pattern.
derivation: The soul is defined as an information pattern (HS.1).
Therefore, the soul is real and conserved.
The soul is localized in the chi-field (HS.2), making it distinct and personal.
The soul persists through time (HS.3), as it changes but does not cease.
Personal identity is the continuity of the soul pattern (HS.4).
Since information is conserved, the soul survives physical death (HS.5).
canonical_node.action: Treat the soul as a real, localized, persistent information pattern; affirm personal identity and survival of death based on this model.
boundary: Does not claim the soul is a material substance.
Does not claim the soul is a universal consciousness.
Does not claim to provide empirical detection methods.
Does not claim to explain the mechanism of soul-body interaction.
test: Check that the soul is defined as an information pattern, not a substance.
Verify that localization is asserted to distinguish individual souls.
Confirm that persistence is defined as continuity, not immutability.
Ensure that identity is tied to soul continuity, not body or memory.
Check that death survival is derived from information conservation.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a model of personal identity and survival of death based on information patterns in the chi-field.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the reality of the self against eliminativism, no-self doctrines, and bundleism.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this axiom, the framework loses a coherent account of personal identity and continuity after death.

overstatement_risks: Claims survival of death based on information conservation without empirical evidence.
Equates soul with information pattern without rigorous definition.
Uses self-reference arguments that may be fallacious.
Relies on theological assertions as support.
kill_conditions: If information is not conserved in the relevant sense.
If the soul pattern is not shown to be localized or persistent.
If personal identity can be explained without a soul pattern.

plain_summary: This document argues that the soul is a real, localized, persistent information pattern in a fundamental field, and that this pattern constitutes personal identity and survives death. It critiques eliminativism, no-self doctrines, and bundleism, but the arguments are largely philosophical and theological, lacking empirical or formal proof.
